subject.title: fix(cli): prevent policy-blocked plugin enable mutations

question: Should the CLI/plugin owner approve the fail-before-mutation policy gate once the branch is refreshed against current `main` and required checks finish?
rationale: The patch changes persisted-config safety behavior correctly and has direct proof, but the protected `maintainer` label requires explicit human handling rather than automatic disposition.

options.title: Approve the narrow safety fix
options.body: Confirm that a policy rejection must never select slots, write configuration, or refresh registry state, then merge after final checks pass.

options.title: Request a broader plugin-control-plane decision
options.body: Pause this PR only if maintainers want the related manifest or canonicalization work reviewed as one combined policy change rather than as separate fixes.

recommendation.title: Approve the narrow safety fix
recommendation.body: Confirm that a policy rejection must never select slots, write configuration, or refresh registry state, then merge after final checks pass.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the available direct contact for the focused CLI implementation and its supplied real-behavior proof; prior-area ownership could not be established from the read-only inspection available here.
